Milestone: Investigate the shared two-map Pygame brief
Activity: Compare two themes, select one and identify player needs, fixed scope, exclusions and prerequisite preparation. All themes retain the same Year 12 game core.
Evidence check: Explain the two-map requirement and why no specialist theme mechanics or extra project periods are added.

Milestone: Design actors, maps, dictionaries and game states
Activity: Design Actor/Player/Hazard responsibilities, independent tile-map lists, item metadata dictionary, state transitions, file contracts and measurable acceptance criteria.
Evidence check: Show state/class/data sketches with the same requirements IDs as the common game contract.

Milestone: Desk-check search, sort and map-transition algorithms
Activity: Write pseudocode for active-item linear search, a taught history-score sort, collision consequences and map completion/loss precedence. Predict boundary, invalid and empty-history outcomes.
Evidence check: Design checkpoint: justify algorithms and trace a duplicate score, missing item, final-map result and zero-time completion.

Milestone: Build actor interfaces and load the supplied maps
Activity: Implement the small actor hierarchy and validate two independent 8 × 10 maps using the supplied tile codes/start/exit rules. Separate game state from drawing.
Evidence check: Show independent map/object state and a concrete malformed-map rejection without silently inventing a map.

Milestone: Implement movement, walls and overridden actor updates
Activity: Implement shared movement/bounds and appropriate Player/Hazard update overrides. Use supplied deterministic patrols and primitive geometry.
Evidence check: Test a wall/boundary move and demonstrate that updating one actor does not mutate another actor accidentally.

Milestone: Implement collection, hazards and active timers
Activity: Build once-only collection, lives, respawn/protection, score and active-play timer rules with the common fixed counts.
Evidence check: Checkpoint: test repeated collection, protected/unprotected hits and loss-before-completion precedence.

Milestone: Integrate dictionary lookup and history-score ordering
Activity: Use the item-ID metadata dictionary and student-written linear search. Implement a taught sort for up to ten valid history scores without confusing record identity with position.
Evidence check: Test missing IDs, duplicate scores, empty history and sorted output; retain the intended original state where required.

Milestone: Integrate map progression and persistent results
Activity: Connect map 1 completion to map 2, carry score/lives, refresh the 90-second map timer, and append one final score. Handle missing/malformed history and failed writes.
Evidence check: Build checkpoint: demonstrate transition state and once-only final save under documented file policies.

Milestone: Integrate instructions, HUD, pause and restart
Activity: Finish title/play/pause/result controls, readable feedback and full restart across both maps. Check relative paths and primitive asset fallbacks before freezing a test version.
Evidence check: Demonstrate pause across a long wall-clock interval and restart restoring initial map, score, lives, time and objects.

Milestone: Run common acceptance cases and regression checks
Activity: Run unit/integration and shared acceptance tests, record actual state/output, repair one cause at a time and repeat earlier passing cases.
Evidence check: Show map validation, OOP/search/sort, transition, timer and file evidence; mark unrun quality checks pending.

Milestone: Run the player and named-machine quality trial
Activity: Use a peer instruction-only trial and the common reliability/usability/response checks on the nominated school setup. Record limitations, source/asset checks and retests.
Evidence check: Justify the outcome with observed evidence rather than claiming universal performance or complete approval.

Milestone: Demonstrate, restore and evaluate the two-map game
Activity: Explain the actor hierarchy, independent maps, dictionary, student search/sort and file policy. Restore a saved version and hand over evidence, evaluation and retrospective.
Evidence check: Evaluate every common FR/NFR ID under the school-issued conditions; explain one limitation and a feasible improvement.
